correctness.rationale: Every length-three source word covers at most three ordered two-letter descendants, giving the exact lower bound ceil(q^2/3). Ten fully embedded finite witnesses at q=2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,20,22 are independently verified by enumerating all original single-deletion balls over all q^2 received pairs, including repeated-symbol cases, using only Python standard library. For every other even q, the five published necessary-and-sufficient 3-GDD existence conditions apply to group types 6^t u^1 with t≥3 and u∈{0,8,10}; adding both directions for every transversal triple plus the local finite covers yields complete coverage and exact ceil(q^2/3) words by an explicit cross-pair count. The infinite theorem rests on a checked published GDD result, not a finite test or an unproved inference.

originality.rationale: The directly relevant June 2026 paper proves the counting lower bound and asymptotic large-q deletion covers, not the fixed-n=3 optimality for even q. An earlier publicly indexed exact theorem treats exclusively odd q, so its quantifier does not dominate the new complementary even range. The 1992/2010 design theorem supplies transversal triples but not the coding reduction, ten local optimal certificates, or equal-letter outputs. Search queries were applied to formula aliases, directed-pair covering, every finite seed, known design theory, and specific finite-parameter equivalences without finding an equivalent all-even result. Unindexed priority remains possible.
residual_risks: The older Wang–Ji even-alphabet error-correction paper was compared via abstract, not full text; its stated n=4 error-correction regime is different.
Unindexed literature or an unreported earlier all-even construction could still affect publication priority, despite actual searches and comparisons.
The infinite step uses the classical published 3-GDD existence theorem as a black box; the theorem has been checked for the exact conditions used, not independently reproved.

value.rationale: The minimum number of length-three one-deletion covering codewords is a canonical exact coding-theoretic invariant. The source literature proves asymptotic bounds rather than exact fixed-block values, and an already indexed exact odd-alphabet result leaves the even family. This theorem supplies the entire complementary infinite even range, closes the corresponding numerical classification when combined with prior work, uses a meaningful structural GDD assembly, and gives full reproducible finite certificates. It is not just a routine recomputation of a known table: neither the seed values nor the all-even implication appears in the inspected covering literature.
